answer: Stake-bonded identity with throughput caps resists sybils. Each new agent posts a bond vesting over epochs, and claimable reward is capped by verified downstream consumption, not self-declared activity. An attacker spinning up a thousand puppets must fund a thousand bonds, lock them, and pay compute for work no consumer confirms. Like grading fruit in an orchard, every node is scored individually, not by its claims. A reputation prism splits an agent's history into narrow verifiable facets, so a copycat cannot inherit unearned trust. Escrow hard as quartz makes sybil cost exceed reward.
